skip_reason: Not a sales call. This is a post-move damage claim intake on an already-completed move: the customer (Ann Gill, a repeat customer on her 3rd or 4th move) reports a dented washing machine front, a broken crystal stem and a broken crystal glass. Khevan's entire role on the call is explaining the in-house customer experience team's damage claim process and texting/emailing her the Monday.com claim form link. No quote, no pricing, no estimate, no booking, no new move discussed at any point. Claims and post-move service recovery calls are explicit skips.
top_strength: Clean, confident claims handling. He set expectations without being asked: in-house customer experience team, not outsourced, one to three business days to first contact, and the three possible outcomes (repair, replace, or settlement). He removed friction on the form itself, offering text and email and answering her real worry before she had to press it: 'No, this is just a simple plug and play form,' plus the reassurance that duplicate submissions get patched together by contact number. He also pre-empted confusion about the Monday.com branding, and closed by thanking her for 'allowing us the opportunity to get things sorted out for you.'
coaching_note: Nothing to coach on the sales rubric, this is a claims call. Two things for Amanda on the claims side rather than the rep. First, the reported damage is to a washing machine that our crew hooked up, and the customer only found the dent after it started banging during a spin cycle. Appliance hookup plus a concealed dent found days later is worth a look on scope and liability, not just as a routine claim. Second, she asked for the link to go to both her and her husband and Khevan only had one email and one phone number on the profile, so it went to her alone. Small thing, but on a fourth-time repeat customer it is worth having secondary contacts on file. Khevan also volunteered a real detail: our crew could not locate the TV mounting screws, and the customer had to hire someone else to source them. That is a hardware-bag process gap on the move itself.
phone_presence_notes: Warm and unhurried throughout with genuine acknowledgment rather than defensiveness, and the customer ended up volunteering her loyalty ('this was our fourth move with you, we're loyal customers and still are'), though he never once used her name.
